name: PowerShell
scope: A person with BASIC proficiency level in PowerShell as a competency should be able to write and read PowerShell Core (pwsh) scripts that automate everyday operational tasks on Linux or Windows: declaring and using variables, arrays and hashtables; writing if/elseif/else, switch, foreach and while constructs; defining simple functions with parameters and validation attributes; and composing cmdlets on the object pipeline (Get-ChildItem, Where-Object, Sort-Object, Group-Object, Select-Object). They can read and write files, work with CSV and JSON via Import-Csv/Export-Csv/ConvertFrom-Json/ConvertTo-Json, compute file hashes, handle errors with try/catch and -ErrorAction, emit warnings and verbose output, and write clean, reusable, well-documented scripts. They can run and debug scripts safely, understand execution basics of pwsh on Linux, and write or fix simple Pester tests for their scripts.
long_scope:
**Competency Scope for PowerShell - BASIC Proficiency**

### 1. Core Language and Syntax
- Variables, arrays, hashtables; string interpolation and quoting rules
- Control flow: if/elseif/else, switch, foreach, while, break/continue
- Simple functions with named parameters, default values, and [Validate*] attributes
- Comparison and logical operators; -match/-like and basic regular expressions

### 2. The Object Pipeline
- Composing cmdlets with the pipeline instead of parsing text
- Where-Object, Sort-Object, Group-Object, Select-Object, Measure-Object
- Building results as PSCustomObjects and exporting them

### 3. Files and Data Formats
- Get-ChildItem, Copy-Item, Move-Item, Remove-Item, Test-Path, New-Item
- Import-Csv / Export-Csv; ConvertFrom-Json / ConvertTo-Json
- Get-Content / Set-Content, Get-FileHash, Compress-Archive

### 4. Error Handling and Robustness
- try/catch/finally, -ErrorAction, error preference variables
- Write-Warning / Write-Verbose / Write-Error; non-crashing handling of malformed input
- Parameter validation so scripts fail fast with clear messages

### 5. Testing and Operational Hygiene
- Running scripts with pwsh on Linux; cross-platform pitfalls (paths, case sensitivity)
- Reading and fixing simple Pester tests; writing basic Describe/It blocks
- Dry-run (-WhatIf-style) switches; idempotent, re-runnable scripts
